title: Descriptive statistics
note: Statistics use the analysis panel. Continuous financial ratios are winsorized at the 1st and 99th percentiles. Expense values not reported remain missing. Compustat sales and earnings are in millions and employment is in thousands; per-employee monetary measures are therefore thousands of USD per employee.
plain: This table shows what a typical company-year looks like and how much companies differ. Different observation counts reflect missing financial variables, not zeros filled in for unavailable data.

title: Subsequent firm growth
note: Entries are coefficients on perceived ghost intensity, with firm-clustered standard errors in parentheses. All models include firm and year effects. The main measure uses a 10-review empirical Bayes prior based on past firm information, using other firm-periods closed by the actual fiscal year-end when the firm has no earlier reviews. The raw share is reported separately. Core controls are size, ROA, PPE/assets, leverage, book-to-market, and the current outcome where appropriate. Log assets are omitted for log revenue and log book equity. Additional controls include dividends, R&D, capital expenditure, advertising, and lagged loss, with duplicate variables removed. * p<0.10; ** p<0.05; *** p<0.01. Samples differ across outcomes and control sets.
plain: We ask whether a company has a different outcome next year when more of its applicants report a ghost-job experience. A negative coefficient means the two move in opposite directions after the stated adjustments. It does not establish that ghost recruitment caused the outcome. More controls can also reduce the sample substantially.

title: Visibility, monitoring, and investment
note: Dependent variable is next-year capital expenditure/assets. Corresponding moderator main effects are included. The ghost coefficient is evaluated at moderator zero; the interaction describes how that association changes with the moderator. These are conditional investment associations, not estimates of which firms post more ghost jobs.
plain: This asks whether the investment relationship differs for larger companies, companies followed by more analysts, or companies with more debt. The interaction is a difference in the relationship; it is not a count of fake advertisements.

title: Alternative definitions and timing checks
rows: No follow-up and ghosting: two points
Firms with at least ten observed years
Full-firm prior and quarter adjustment (timing sensitivity)
note: Unless noted, outcome is next-year capital expenditure/assets with core controls. Feature variants use raw shares so they can be compared to the raw-share column of the growth table. Main smoothed estimates are used for sample restrictions. Centered windows and full-sample priors can use future information and are measurement sensitivities, not forward prediction tests. The placebo uses prior capital expenditure and additional controls. Omit-one-firm tests use the main smoothed specification. Lower/upper bounds set unresolved reviews to zero/one only for the stated bounds and retain their company-years.
plain: These checks ask whether the conclusion depends on one definition, thin review coverage, the pandemic period, or a single company. A result that changes with the definition needs a narrower interpretation. A relationship with past investment can also point to timing or reverse-causality concerns.

title: Determinants, peers, and cost adjustment

Change in pension expense per worker ($000s) × sales-change interaction
Change in pension expense / sales × sales-change interaction
Current net employment change: core controls
Current net employment change: full controls
note: The determinant model has raw ghost share as the outcome and firm/year effects. Time-invariant industry status may be absorbed; the selected-SIC high-tech proxy is not occupation skill. Peer tests use leave-one-out two-digit SIC/year shares. Cost tests include absolute annual differences and percentage-change sensitivities. The absolute-difference cost controls are ROA, log assets, capital expenditure, and advertising. Pension/retirement expense (XPR) is distinct from staff expense (XLR). The same-year employment specifications retain employee levels and the stated core/full controls. A positive interaction multiplied by a negative sales change makes a negative contribution; it does not automatically imply milder cuts.
plain: These tests separate three questions: which company characteristics accompany the measure, whether firms’ experiences move with their industry peers, and how costs and headcount change when sales change. They do not turn the main comparison into a causal experiment.

title: Additional tests: data and identification limits
rows: Not estimated as a causal test: common industry shocks and the leave-one-out peer algebra do not establish an exclusion restriction.
No independent employee satisfaction or worker-flow file supplied; net employment is reported separately.
No RepRisk or employee-related ESG outcome file supplied.
Review sample does not identify the national share of ghost vacancies; no scaled vacancy correction estimated.
note: All estimable tests and model failures are recorded in the downloadable model-status file. Independent human validation of the classifier remains outstanding.
plain: A missing source is not a zero result. Net headcount cannot stand in for employee departures, and a peer measure does not become a valid causal instrument just because it leaves the focal firm out.
